floor.name: Open water
floor.text: Open water, two metres deep and clear to the bottom. A swimmer goes past on her back, looking up at the far bank instead of where she's going. At half a g the waves from the jetty come in slow and tall, a long breath apart.

floor.name: The elders' hour
floor.text: Lamp-dawn, and this water belongs to the elders. A dozen heads move slowly through the grey, two by two, talking. Someone well over a hundred swims a careful breaststroke and stops halfway to watch the far bank come up. By nine they're out, and the children are coming.

floor.name: A swimming lane
floor.text: A lane roped along the axis, twelve hundred metres from shore to shore. A club swimmer touches the rope and turns, and the coach on a float calls her time, bright and thin in the heliox. Races go lengthwise. Across, the far shore is a quarter of the way round the drum, and looks it.

floor.name: The shallows
floor.text: A shelf of shallows by the shore, knee-deep and warm by afternoon. Small children from the Low decks sit in it and splash, and at half a g every splash goes nearly twice as high as at home and hangs there. A parent stands guard with a robe over one arm.

floor.name: A float
floor.text: A wooden float moored in open water, big enough for ten. People swim out, lie on it face up and watch the far bank, where the grounds hang overhead and somebody is running the heavy bend. It rocks a little on its chain when the slow waves come through.

floor.name: The lake after dusk
floor.text: Dark water. The lake closes at dusk, and the only light on it is the far bank's pavilion lamps and the flyers' hand lamps along the axis, laid on the surface in long wobbling lines. A cleaning robot works along the shore, collecting a towel, a sandal and somebody's lid.

floor.name: A row in blossom
floor.text: A row in blossom, white and pale pink, smelling faintly sweet. Three volunteers on step-ladders work along it with soft brushes, flower to flower, tree to tree, carrying pollen the way nothing else in Sorrel can. One has a stitch on her sleeve for every row she's brushed.

floor.name: A winter tent
floor.text: A tent of grey cloth over six rows of bare trees, held at four degrees. There's a queue at the flap, and people coming out pink-cheeked and delighted, breathing on their hands to watch their breath. Inside, the trees are asleep and the ground is brown with fallen leaves.

floor.name: A picking crew
floor.text: A picking crew with canvas bags and short ladders, working a row from both ends. Each apple is lifted and twisted, never pulled, and laid one deep in a padded crate. An apple dropped at half a g lands softly and a little anti, and is still counted as bruised.

floor.name: Between the rows
floor.text: Mown grass between two rows of trees in full leaf. The light comes straight down all day, so each tree's shadow sits under it like a dark pool and never moves. A family from {hour} has spread a cloth here, which is allowed, and is eyeing the apples, which aren't.

floor.name: A grafting bench
floor.text: A grafting bench under a tree: knives, tape, and a basket of cut twigs in wet cloth. An old grafter joins a twig to a young rootstock with three cuts and a wrap, and writes a number on its tag. Every tree here is a copy of a copy, and she knows whose.

floor.name: Pruning
floor.text: A section after picking, the trees bare, and a pruning crew taking out the crossing branches. The cuttings go in neat bundles to the wood-turners, who make spoons, pegs and chair rungs from apple wood, which smells sweet under the lathe and lasts a lifetime or three.

floor.name: A picnic
floor.text: A picnic on a blue cloth: crackers, hard cheese, a Mill-sugar cake and six lidded crocks, opened one at a time and closed again. Somebody's grandfather is asleep with his jacket over his eyes. The children lie on their backs, pointing at a kite on the far bank, three kilometres up.

floor.name: A kite lane
floor.text: A kite lane marked in white along the axis. A boy walks it backwards, very slowly, paying out line, while a red kite climbs on nothing but his walking pace. His sister walks beside him giving advice he hasn't asked for, and is mostly right.

floor.name: Open lawn
floor.text: Open lawn, short and springy, with nothing on it but people. A couple are trying cartwheels, which at half a g take long enough to change your mind halfway round. A game of catch drifts past, the throws dipping one way and sailing the other.

floor.name: Under a big tree
floor.text: A big plane tree, the only one for a hundred metres, with a ring of people in its shade. At noon even the shade is brighter than any room in the drum. Somebody is reading aloud, somebody is asleep, and somebody is quietly eating the last pastry.

floor.name: Signal cloths
floor.text: Two families have laid long cloths on the grass in letters twenty metres high, spelling a greeting to cousins on the far bank. Overhead, three kilometres up and upside down, the cousins are laying out their answer. It's a little crooked. Everyone agrees it's readable.

floor.name: End of a turn
floor.text: The end of a turn. The line has gone warm as it eases down, cloths are being shaken out, and children are being told it's time, twice. The pavilion's chime has sounded. Nobody hurries: the next decks are already coming up behind them.

floor.name: A spinball pitch
floor.text: A spinball pitch, and a school team from {hour} learning the half-g break. A throw spinward dives into the turf a third heavier; one thrown anti sails over everyone's heads. The coach shouts angles and the children shout back. At this weight everyone is surprised every time.

floor.name: A heavy bend
floor.text: The heavy bend of a running track, where a sprinter heading spinward weighs a fifth more and feels it in the knees. A coach with a board stands at the apex, watching who slows down. Everyone does. The good ones do it later.

floor.name: A long-jump pit
floor.text: A long-jump pit twice the length of the old ones, raked smooth, with the runway along the axis so the jumps fly true. A girl lands a long way down it in a slow spray of sand, and a man with a tape measures it twice to be sure.

floor.name: A practice field
floor.text: A practice field where a club is learning to catch at half a g. High balls hang so long that three people get under each one. Somebody has chalked HEAVY and LIGHT on the grass with arrows, for the newcomers, and the newcomers are standing on them.

floor.name: The stands
floor.text: Low timber stands along a pitch, half full. Elders sit at the top, where it's quietest, with lidded cups and opinions. A match is on below, and every time a throw goes anti and sails, the whole stand leans the same way to follow it.

floor.name: The kit shed
floor.text: A long shed of balls, nets, hurdles and spikes, all old and all mended. The keeper writes your name and deck in a book and lends you anything, and knows by the end of the day which decks bring things back.

floor.name: A yew walk
floor.text: A walk between old yews, dark green and dense, where the light comes in at a slant from the Hollow side. The shadows here lean toward the end wall all day. It's quiet enough to hear your own steps, which in heliox sound small and bright.

floor.name: A shade garden
floor.text: A shade garden of ferns and moss under a canopy of hornbeam. The ferns stand taller than people at half a g, and every frond leans the same way, toward the line. A gardener kneels on a pad, taking out weeds one at a time, in no hurry at all.

floor.name: Bamboo
floor.text: A stand of bamboo three storeys high, thin and straight at half a g, with a path through it just wide enough for two. Couples come here at dusk. When someone hurries through, the stems knock together with a bright hollow clatter that carries in the heliox.

floor.name: The wood path at night
floor.text: A path through the wood after dusk, lit by low lamps at about a corridor's brightness. Somebody ahead is singing under their breath. Through the branches a line of flyers' hand lamps drifts along the axis, and the far bank's path lamps make a ring that climbs and meets above you.

floor.name: The woodwarden's hut
floor.text: A woodwarden's hut with fallen branches stacked outside, sorted by length for the turners. The warden lends hand lamps for the evening paths, takes names, and will tell you, if you ask, which tree is the oldest. It's always the one you're standing next to.

floor.name: Where the light falls away
floor.text: Here the Hollow's light starts to fall away toward the wall. At noon you can feel it change over a few hundred paces: the grass behind you bright, the trees ahead already like evening. People choose their spot by how much evening they want.

floor.name: A pavilion
floor.text: A cab pavilion: a round roof on pillars, a ring of benches, a drinking fountain, and doors that open every few seconds on another family stepping out and looking straight up. A small boy stands frozen on the threshold, mouth open, until his mother moves him gently aside.

floor.name: Allotments
floor.text: Allotment beds behind a low hedge: beans, chard, salad leaves, a row of strawberries under net, all lit free by the line. Each bed belongs to a block from {hour} and is worked on its turn. The beds are tidiest just before a turn ends, when the next block arrives to look.

floor.name: A gravel path
floor.text: A gravel path between pavilions, worn smooth by turns. Walking is slow up here, a little over a metre a second, and nobody minds. A woman pushes a very old man in a chair, and he points out where things used to be. Most of them still are.

floor.name: Mowers at night
floor.text: After the floor closes, the mowers come out: low robots working in straight lines through the lamp-night, trimming and sweeping and picking up whatever a turn left behind. This one has found a shoe, a lid and a child's drawing of the far bank, and takes them to the pavilion's lost box.

floor.name: A drinking fountain
floor.text: A stone drinking fountain by the path. At half a g its arc stands twice as high as the ones at home, and Low-deck children keep bending to where the water ought to be and getting it in the eye.

floor.name: Long grass
floor.text: A strip of long grass left unmown, full of clover, poppies and seed heads that stand taller at half a g than anywhere in the drum. A sign asks you to keep to the path. Somebody's little sister is lying in the middle of it, out of sight, looking up.

floor.name: A turn arriving
floor.text: A pavilion's doors keep opening: a Low-deck turn is arriving, a few hundred families in ten minutes, spreading out over the grass. Within a quarter of an hour every one of them has looked up, pointed, and found something on the far bank to argue about.

floor.name: A memorial bench
floor.text: A bench with a small brass plate: a name, two dates, and the words she liked it here. A bench in the Hollow is the dearest memorial in Sorrel, and there's a waiting list. Today a family is sitting on it eating pastries, which is what it's for.

floor.name: A herb bed
floor.text: A long herb bed beside the path: mint, thyme, sorrel and chives, lit free by the line. Anyone on a turn may pick one sprig, and the bed is planted thick because of it. Children walk its length rubbing leaves between their fingers and making each other smell them.

floor.name: Full noon
floor.text: Full noon: a hundred thousand lux straight down, and a line too bright to look at. Every shadow is a short dark patch right under its owner, sharp on its spinward and anti sides and blurred toward the ends of the drum. It will stay exactly there until three.

wall.name: A lower tier
wall.text: A lower tier, not far above the floor and a little lighter than it. Terrace flats look out over a path of worn stone, each door with a pot of herbs and a chair. An old man in one of the chairs is reading the far bank through field glasses, a page at a time.

wall.name: Terrace flats
wall.text: A row of terrace flats, the only homes in Sorrel with windows on the Hollow. Every window has a chair pulled up to it. The residents are the oldest people in the drum, and the handrail runs unbroken the whole length of the tier, polished by their hands.

wall.name: The tier stair
wall.text: A long stair between tiers, cut into the wall, with a rail on both sides and a landing every forty steps. Going up, every step weighs a little less than the last. People who climb it daily swear they can feel the difference between landings. They can't, quite.

wall.name: Espaliered figs
wall.text: A terrace garden of figs and plums trained flat against the riser, their branches pinned to wires. The tier gets a little under half the floor's light, which suits them, and the gardener on her ladder reaches the top branches in one easy step at this weight.

wall.name: A tea hatch
wall.text: A tea counter in a niche of the riser: three stools and a hatch, serving tea in lidded cups to people resting on the climb. The owner has watched the Hollow from this hatch for forty years and will tell you which far-bank pavilion is busiest without looking up.

wall.name: A promenade
wall.text: A promenade along the tier, right round the wall, with benches facing the Hollow. The floor spreads out below and climbs away on both sides until it's overhead, with the lake hanging somewhere off on its side. People walk it slowly in {hour} colours, stopping to point.

wall.name: A leaping lawn
wall.text: A strip of lawn at about a third of a g, where a standing jump clears a metre and a half and every landing comes down a hand's width spinward. Three teenagers are practising a reel, and their line has crept several metres along the tier since they began.

wall.name: Chairs for a wedding
wall.text: Rows of borrowed chairs going out along the tier, no two alike, the oldest at the front. A wedding is set for dusk. Someone's aunt is pinning cloth to a trellis, someone's uncle is counting the gin, and the apple sits in a lidded box, guarded by a child.

wall.name: A tier kitchen
wall.text: A kitchen in the riser, cooking for the tier. Bubbles rise slowly at a third of a g, so the soup pots seem to think about boiling for a long time before they do. Everything goes out under a lid, as everywhere, and cools on the walk to your bench anyway.

wall.name: Stopping mats
wall.text: Soft mats laid along the tier for a school visit. At about a quarter of a g your feet grip a quarter as well, so the lesson is stopping: lean back early, small steps, lots of room. A class from {hour} is skidding past the teacher in a slow, delighted line.

wall.name: A rose walk
wall.text: A walk of climbing roses on arches, grown so long and loose at this weight that they meet overhead. The light here is still nearly half the floor's. A couple sits in the middle of the walk with a flask between them, and everyone passing finds something else to look at.

wall.name: A porter's path
wall.text: A goods path along the tier, where a porter wheels a cart of plant pots. At this weight he could lift the cart, but it's no easier to stop, so he walks it slowly and takes the corners wide. Pushed spinward, he says, it feels heavier. He's right, by about a twentieth.

wall.name: A jumping lawn
wall.text: A lawn where people jump just to see. At this height a standing jump clears three metres or so, hangs for several seconds and comes down a long stride spinward of where it left. Adults who came up for the view are, without exception, jumping.

wall.name: Hanging strawberries
wall.text: Strawberry troughs hung along the riser, their runners trailing down a whole storey because so little pulls them. The berries are small and the leaves are huge. Tier children water them on a rota and are paid in strawberries, which they consider fair.

wall.name: The bright face
wall.text: A tier of benches facing down the Hollow. The wall's faces catch their most light around this height, more than at the foot, because they look straight down the line. Elders who know it sit with their backs to the riser and their eyes shut, getting the best of it.

wall.name: The Tenth
wall.text: A tier at about a tenth of a g, where a jump goes four or five metres up, takes six seconds and lands a couple of metres spinward. The light is down to a quarter or a third of the floor's, and the gardens have turned to shade plants: ferns, hostas, tea.

wall.name: A garden path
wall.text: A garden path round the tier. At this height walking spinward makes you a tenth heavier or more, and walking back as much lighter, so gardeners carry full cans anti and come back empty the other way. Everyone who works up here walks with the same slight lean.

wall.name: A quiet tier
wall.text: A quiet tier of benches and moss, far enough up that the floor's crowds are only a sound. People come here to sit and look along the Hollow, which from up here runs away like the inside of a lit pipe, floor on every side.

wall.name: A top garden
wall.text: A top garden at well under a tenth of a g, lit mostly by the Hollow's own glow. Beans climb strings toward the axis and keep going. A dropped trowel takes nearly two seconds to land, a hand's width anti. A child jumps the height of a house and lands in the squash.

wall.name: Under the netting
wall.text: The last tier below the flying hall. Not far overhead the netting begins, and beyond it people swim the air in wing-sleeves, slow and lengthwise. Gardeners up here work in a sort of hover: every step is a small leap, and they tie their tools to their belts.

wall.name: A spinward basket
wall.text: A picking path where walking spinward makes you a fifth heavier or more, and walking anti as much lighter. Pickers carry full baskets anti and walk back empty. A visitor who hasn't been told walks spinward with a full basket and stops halfway, puzzled.
